subject: [Reliability Program] Incident bot rollout update: staged enablement + approvals needed
related_links: Confluence: Incident bot usage and escalation guidelines
Confluence: Incident bot context bundles spec
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 8:17 AM PT
Subject: [Reliability Program] Incident bot rollout update: staged enablement + approvals needed
Attachments: incident-bot-rollout-checklist_v3.pdf; incident-bot-context-bundle-mvp_notes_2025-02-14.docx

Neha,

Quick rollout update on the “incident bot + diagnostics improvements” workstream. We’re ready to move from limited beta to broader enablement, but we need 2 approvals from leadership to do it safely.

Where we are (current state)
- Bot posts an initial “context bundle” into #incidents threads:
  1) recent deploys/rollouts (service/version/region + links)
  2) config diffs (routing policy + feature flags; redaction enforced)
  3) saturation snapshot (queue depth/throttling/scheduler contention) + links to canonical dashboards
- Fail-open behavior: collectors time out individually and still render a partial bundle with explicit “data unavailable” sections.
- Beta is enabled for a small subset of SRE rotation channels + a couple of services. Early feedback is positive on deploy context; config diffs were the main gap.

Proposed staged rollout (starting next week)
Phase A (Mon–Tue): Expand to all SRE on-call rotations (still limited channel allowlist)
- Enable feature flag for all on-call rotations (SRE primary + secondary) to reduce “why doesn’t it work for us?” friction.
- Keep channel allowlist limited to incident channels only (#incidents + #incidents-<region>) to avoid noise.

Phase B (Wed–Fri): Default-on in #incidents for Sev0/Sev1, with restricted-mode enforcement
- For “restricted incidents” (customer-sensitive), bot posts minimal metadata in #incidents and posts the full bundle in the restricted channel (current design).
- Add a short command in-thread to request deeper diagnostics (still human-in-the-loop).

Phase C (following week): Broader enablement + hygiene work
- Tune time windows and formatting based on early-week feedback.
- Track adoption and reliability metrics (MTTR proxy + time-to-suspect-change).

Key risks / what we’re doing about them
1) Noise / thread spam
- Single bundle on incident open + one refresh if incident duration > 30m (rate-limited).
- Formatting: compact blocks, collapsible “details” sections, consistent timestamps.

2) Data sensitivity (accidentally posting customer payloads / secrets)
- Hard redaction rules and allowlisted config keys.
- “Restricted mode” routes full bundle to a restricted channel.
- Audit logging of what the bot posted (key names + classification, not raw values).

3) Load / reliability of collectors during incidents
- Collector timeouts (per collector) + concurrency limits.
- Caching keyed by incident id + time window.
- Metrics collector degrades gracefully if metrics backend lags.

4) Misleading “suspected change” heuristics
- We’re framing as “possible correlated change(s)” (not causal), only when deploy/config deltas overlap incident start window.
- We’ll keep this behind a separate flag for now.

Approvals needed (to proceed with Phase A/B)
1) Leadership approval to enable bot by default for all SRE rotations (Phase A) and to post automatically in #incidents for Sev0/Sev1 (Phase B).
2) Security sign-off that the current restricted-mode/redaction approach is acceptable for this broader rollout (we can do a final quick pass early next week).

If you’re comfortable, I’ll send:
- a short #eng announcement + “how to give feedback” instructions
- a go/no-go checklist for on-call leads

Attachments:
- Rollout checklist v3 (includes rollback criteria + monitoring)
- MVP bundle notes (examples of good vs noisy output)

Thanks,
Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Incident workflow owner | SRE
Redwood Inference


On Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Re: [Reliability Program] Incident bot rollout update: staged enablement + approvals needed

Sean,

Thanks for the crisp summary.

I’m supportive of moving to Phase A/B with two conditions:
1) We need explicit rollback criteria that the on-call lead can execute without debate (e.g., “bot posting causes X messages/min” or “collector error rate > Y%”).
2) I want the restricted-mode behavior to be unambiguous: it should be impossible for a responder to accidentally “request more context” in a public channel and have sensitive diffs posted there.

Can you reply with:
- the exact go/no-go / rollback triggers you plan to use
- confirmation that the “request more context” command is disabled (or safely routed) in unrestricted channels

If those are covered, consider this approval for Phase A/B. For security sign-off, I’ll treat it as required before Phase B (default posting in #incidents), but we can start Phase A while the final review is in flight.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Exec Sponsor, Reliability Program
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 14, 2025 at 11:36 AM PT
Subject: Re: [Reliability Program] Incident bot rollout update: staged enablement + approvals needed

Neha,

Agreed on both conditions. Details below.

Rollback / go-no-go triggers (on-call lead owned; immediate disable via feature flag)
We’ll publish these in the rollout checklist and in the on-call channel pin:
- Noise trigger: >2 bot posts per incident thread within 30 minutes (excluding explicit /bot refresh) OR >10 bot messages/hour in #incidents.
- Reliability trigger: bot bundle render latency p95 > 20s for 30 minutes OR collector timeout rate > 15% over 1 hour.
- Safety trigger: any report of a redaction miss / sensitive value posted (immediate disable + incident review).
- Load trigger: metrics backend elevated error rate attributable to bot traffic (we’ll watch the dashboards; bot traffic is tagged).

Restricted-mode + “request more context” safety
- The “request more context” command is gated:
  - In normal incidents: it only returns links (dashboards/runbooks) unless the incident channel is allowlisted.
  - In restricted incidents: the command response in #incidents is always a stub (“additional context available in restricted channel”) and the full output is only posted in the restricted channel.
- We’ll add a loud visual indicator in the Slack block header when restricted mode is active.

Next steps
- I’ll kick off Phase A Monday AM (enable for all SRE rotations; allowlisted incident channels only).
- I’ll schedule the security sign-off checkpoint for early next week before Phase B.
- I’ll send you the final #eng announcement text for review (1 paragraph + how to report false positives/noise).

Thanks,
Sean
